differences.note: Inside a rotated or transformed box (\rotatebox, a landscape page), pdfTeX computes a link target's position from leftover memory instead of the target itself, so the link lands somewhere unrelated, often far above the page. PhiTeX sends the link to the target. The pages themselves are identical; only where these links point differs.

edit.note: Every edit's PDF is byte-identical to TeX Live's rebuild of the edited document, except in Grail. There, hyperxmp writes the time the .log file was saved into the PDF's metadata, so no two TeX Live builds of it are the same. With that time fixed, TeX Live's PDF of the unedited paper is identical to PhiTeX's.

method: Clean builds, one thread, on one machine. TeX Live's time is the whole job a latexmk user waits for: pdflatex or xelatex run again and again until the document's files stop changing (the last run is the one that confirms it, as latexmk's is), with every BibTeX, biber and makeindex run the document needs between them, their wall times added up. PhiTeX's time is one `phitex build --exact-pdf -j 1` (the release binary), which does all of that itself, from an empty cache. Both start from a fresh copy of the document's sources, with no files from an earlier build, and both start with their formats already made: TeX Live's are in its installation, PhiTeX's were built once before the first document. Each document was built three times by each, the two alternating on the same node, and each time shown is the median of its three. Edits: PhiTeX's time from saving the file to the finished build in `phitex watch` (the median of five tries; one try when it took over 5 s), beside one full rebuild of the edited document by TeX Live, counted as above.
